items.name: Dried amla
items.prabhava: Foremost rasayana — sour taste yet cooling and pitta-pacifying, an exception to rasa rules; contains five tastes (all but salty) and rejuvenates all tissues.
combinations: with honey for kapha
with ghee for pitta
as part of triphala or chyawanprash
contraindications: very low agni without warming spices
items.preparation: Powder stirred into warm water on an empty stomach, or rehydrated; the classical base of chyawanprash.

items.name: Haritaki (chebulic myrobalan)
items.prabhava: Called the mother of remedies — tridoshic despite heating virya; gently scrapes ama and regulates the bowels without weakening them.
combinations: ritu haritaki: taken with a different anupana each season (rock salt in monsoon, jaggery in autumn, ginger in winter…)
as part of triphala
contraindications: acute vata aggravation from fasting or exertion
items.preparation: Powder with warm water at night for regularity; seasonal anupana per the ritu-haritaki tradition.

items.name: Bibhitaki (belleric myrobalan)
items.prabhava: The kapha specialist of the triphala trio — clears the chest and throat, supports the voice, eyes and hair.
combinations: with honey for cough and kapha
as part of triphala
contraindications: strong vata aggravation in high doses
very dry constitutions without an oily anupana
items.preparation: Powder with honey or warm water; traditionally taken after meals for kapha in the head and chest.

items.name: Triphala
items.prabhava: The three fruits in balance — gentle tridoshic bowel regulator and eye rasayana that detoxifies without depleting.
combinations: with warm water at bedtime
with honey in the morning for kapha
with ghee for eye health
items.preparation: One teaspoon steeped in warm water at bedtime; ghee-and-honey (unequal parts) carrier for rasayana use.

items.name: Ashwagandha root powder
items.prabhava: Balya rasayana — builds strength and ojas while calming the mind; one of the few tonics that both grounds vata and supports restful sleep.
combinations: simmered in warm milk with a little ghee and jaggery (classical anupana)
with dates for building
items.preparation: Simmer the powder in milk for a few minutes; take at night for sleep and strength.
items.reviewNote: Bhavaprakasha lists laghu-snigdha gunas; some modern texts call it heavy because of its building action. Laghu retained here.

items.name: Shatavari root powder
items.prabhava: The premier female reproductive rasayana — nourishes rasa dhatu, supports lactation, and soothes pitta in the gut lining.
combinations: simmered in warm milk with cardamom
with ghee for pitta conditions
items.preparation: Simmer in milk or warm water; ghee-fried powder (shatavari ghrita style) for deeper nourishment.

items.name: Guduchi (giloy) stem
items.prabhava: Amrita, the nectar plant — heating yet pitta-pacifying, a rare exception; the classical rasayana for chronic fevers and immunity.
combinations: stem decoction (kwatha) with dry ginger for vata
with jaggery for constipation
contraindications: autoimmune conditions on immunosuppressants (consult a practitioner)
items.preparation: Fresh or dried stem simmered as decoction; powder with warm water for daily rasayana use.

items.name: Giloy satva (starch extract)
items.prabhava: The cooling starch of guduchi — reserved for burning sensations, pitta fevers and debility where the whole stem would be too stimulating.
combinations: with rice water for burning and thirst
with milk for debility after fever
items.preparation: A pinch to half a teaspoon stirred into rice water, milk or cool water.

items.name: Brahmi (bacopa)
items.prabhava: Medhya rasayana — sharpens memory and intellect while cooling an agitated mind; the classical herb of students and meditators.
combinations: with ghee (brahmi ghrita) for the mind
with warm milk
with honey for kapha dullness
contraindications: very low agni (take with warming anupana)
high doses may cause loose stools
items.preparation: Powder in warm water or milk in the morning; ghee-based preparations for sustained medhya effect.

items.name: Gotu kola
items.prabhava: Medhya rasayana named among Charaka's four mind tonics — clarifies the mind and supports the skin and circulation.
combinations: fresh leaves in chutney or juice (South Indian tradition)
with milk as medhya tonic
items.preparation: Fresh leaf juice, chutney, or dried powder in warm water in the morning.

items.name: Shankhpushpi
items.prabhava: Charaka's foremost medhya rasayana — calms mental chatter and supports sleep while strengthening memory.
combinations: with milk at bedtime for restless sleep
with brahmi for study
items.preparation: Whole-plant powder or syrup in warm milk; evening dose for sleep, morning for study.

items.name: Vidari kanda
items.prabhava: Nourishing wild tuber — brimhana and galactagogue, rebuilding tissue in convalescence and postpartum.
combinations: with milk and sugar for weight gain
with ghee for postpartum recovery
items.preparation: Powder simmered in milk; take in the morning when agni is supported.

items.name: Safed musli
items.prabhava: Vrishya rasayana — builds shukra dhatu and vitality; the classical white-tuber aphrodisiac tonic.
combinations: with warm milk and mishri
with ashwagandha for strength
items.preparation: Powder simmered in milk with a little sweetener; classically taken in winter for building.

items.name: Mucuna seed
items.prabhava: Vrishya and nervine tonic — the classical source of natural levodopa; grounds vata deeply when properly processed.
combinations: with warm milk after classical processing (shodhana)
contraindications: raw or unprocessed seed (must undergo shodhana)
items.preparation: Only classically processed (soaked, dehusked, milk-boiled) seed powder is dietary; simmer in milk.

items.name: Gokshura (tribulus)
items.prabhava: Mutrala rasayana — soothes and strengthens the urinary tract; nourishing where most diuretics deplete.
combinations: decoction with coriander for urinary burning
with milk as strength tonic
items.preparation: Fruit powder as decoction or in warm milk; classically paired with cooling herbs for the urinary system.

items.name: Punarnava leaf
items.prabhava: The one that renews — classical anti-edema and kidney rejuvenative; eaten as a seasonal green in parts of India.
combinations: cooked as a green with mild spices
decoction with dry ginger for swelling
items.preparation: Young leaves cooked like other greens; dried leaf as decoction under guidance.
items.reviewNote: Vipaka reported as madhura by most nighantus; some traditions list katu. Madhura retained.

items.name: Moringa leaf powder
items.prabhava: Concentrated shigru leaf — kindles agni, scrapes kapha and ama, and delivers dense micronutrition in small doses.
combinations: stirred into soups, dals or buttermilk
with lemon water in the morning for kapha
contraindications: pregnancy (avoid concentrated doses; leaf as food is traditional)
items.preparation: Add to warm (not boiling) food at the end of cooking to keep its potency.

items.name: Neem leaf
items.prabhava: Krimighna and blood purifier — the intensely bitter leaf that clears heat, skin conditions and parasites; eaten ritually at spring new year.
combinations: a few tender leaves with jaggery at Ugadi/Gudi Padwa
juice with honey for skin (short courses)
contraindications: pregnancy and couples trying to conceive
long continuous use (take in short seasonal courses)
items.preparation: Tender spring leaves in small quantity, fried in ghee or with jaggery; never as a daily staple.

items.name: Neem flower
items.prabhava: Milder than the leaf — the traditional bitter of ugadi pachadi and South Indian spring rasams, clearing pitta and kapha accumulated over winter.
combinations: in ugadi pachadi with jaggery, tamarind, raw mango, salt and chili
dry-roasted over rice with ghee
items.preparation: Fresh or dried flowers dry-roasted or sun-dried; used seasonally in pachadi and flower rasam.

items.name: Aloe vera pulp
items.prabhava: Kumari — rejuvenative for the female reproductive system and liver; the inner gel cools where the leaf latex strongly purges.
combinations: fresh gel with a pinch of turmeric
juice before breakfast for pitta
contraindications: whole-leaf/latex preparations (strong purgative — inner gel only)
items.preparation: Inner leaf gel rinsed of yellow latex, taken fresh; 1–2 tablespoons before food.

items.name: Psyllium husk
items.prabhava: Picchila bulk regulator — soothes the gut lining and works for both constipation and loose stools by absorbing water either way.
combinations: in warm milk at night for constipation
in buttermilk or curd for loose stools
contraindications: take medicines at a separate time (absorption)
items.preparation: Stir into a full glass of warm liquid and drink immediately, followed by more water.

items.name: Wheatgrass
combinations: fresh juice on an empty stomach
powder in water with lemon
contraindications: wheat allergy (usually gluten-free but cross-contamination possible)
items.preparation: Fresh-pressed juice or reconstituted powder, taken on an empty stomach in the morning.

items.name: Spirulina
combinations: blended into smoothies or juice
with lemon to soften the flavor
contraindications: source quality matters (toxin contamination in poor brands)
items.preparation: Powder or tablets with food; start with small doses.

items.name: Chirata
items.prabhava: Jvaraghna bitter tonic — the classical overnight infusion for fevers, skin heat and sluggish liver.
combinations: overnight cold infusion drunk before breakfast
with honey to buffer the bitterness
items.preparation: Steep the dried herb in water overnight; drink the strained infusion on an empty stomach in short courses.

items.name: Kalmegh (andrographis)
items.prabhava: The king of bitters — liver protector and immune support at the first sign of seasonal fevers and colds.
combinations: decoction at the onset of monsoon fevers
with honey after the decoction cools
items.preparation: Short decoction courses of the whole herb; intensely bitter, so dose small.
